messages:
adan: Heads up — after today's kernel-selection refactor I see host CPU on ingress jump ~3-4x for small requests (<1KB). gRPC streaming p50/p95 climbed. Looks like a lot of tiny writev syscalls and tokenization CPU.
marta: saw the same on the canary cluster. pprof points at net.writev + tokenizer.Tokenize hot paths. KV cache miss rate also spiked for the same traffic shape :/ 
adan: confirmed: when we force the pre-refactor kernel policy the numbers go back down. So algo change is the likely trigger.
sahil: my quick diff read: we flipped to latency-first kernel selection for more model variants. For short sequences that reduces batching because the selector prefers single-request low-latency kernels. That would explain smaller batch sizes + more writes.
jun: also noticed the parser now eagerly slices streams per-chunk rather than coalescing multiple small frames. That increases syscall overhead at the host before anything hits GPU.
marta: attaching rough pprof summary (copied):
```
30.1%  net.Writev
21.4%  tokenizer.Tokenize
12.0%  runtime.mallocgc
8.5%   ingress.ParseFrame
6.0%   kvcache.Lookup (miss path)
```
not exact but matches flamegraph.
adan: thanks. also observed increased HTTP/2 HEADERS churn — HPACK encode penalties when we don't coalesce requests (many small writes => header table churn).
sahil: quick mitigation idea: revert kernel-policy flip for small-seq workloads + re-enable stream coalescing. Also add explicit batching floor (min_batch_size=4) for kernels marked latency-first.
jun: agreed. We should also instrument kernel selection decisions in metrics (kernel_policy, chosen_kernel, estimated_batch_size) to see live behavior. Right now it's opaque.
marta: can we try a patch that forces writev coalesce at the proxy layer? simple change: accumulate up to 8 frames or 2ms whichever first, then flush. Might recover most of the host cost with minimal latency impact.
adan: good plan. small A/B to canary: revert policy + proxy coalesce. If that works, we can do more nuanced selector heuristics.
ci-bot: jun/test-kernel-rollback triggered - smoke tests started.
deploy-bot: canary rollback in cluster us-east-2 started by adan.
sahil: followups:
- add metric: redwood_runtime_kernel_policy_choice (string)
- add gauge: ingress_coalesce_buffer_depth
- add trace span around tokenizer -> kvcache lookup to correlate misses
marta: I'll own the proxy coalesce patch, will open a PR in 10m. Need someone to run the canary and collect pprof.
jun: I will run pprof live once PR is up. command I'll use: `pprof -http=:6060 ./profiles/cpu.pprof` and also capture syscall traces: `sudo perf record -e syscalls:sys_enter_writev -a -g -- sleep 30`.
adan: thx. If the rollback + coalesce doesn't fully fix tail we'll consider changing kernel selector to use token-count estimate (tokenize cheaply on host) before choosing kernel so batching heuristics are accurate.
marta: one more note: KV cache thrash looked worst for multitenant small requests — might be eviction policy bias after the refactor. I'll add eviction hit-rate to the KV metrics too.
sahil: ok we have an action list. i'll join the canary watch. :thumbsup:
adan: plan captured. will update thread when we have canary numbers.
